bullets.title: Anthropic's 14x Revenue Surge Validates AI Demand Thesis; S&P 500 Hits ATH
bullets.body: Anthropic reported Q2 revenue of $11.5B (up 14x YoY) and is projecting 2028 revenue of $190–200B vs a $47B run rate in May. OpenAI crossed $40B annualized revenue with 20%+ MoM growth. Goldman Sachs calculates AI infrastructure stocks accounted for roughly half of S&P 500's 31% YoY EPS growth in Q2. S&P 500 reached a new all-time high Thursday with NDX posting a third consecutive weekly gain; SPX futures +0.11% Monday. September Fed hike odds fell to ~31% from ~50% earlier in the week on soft CPI/PPI and retail sales data.

bullets.title: NVDA Cuts OpenAI Ohio Data Center Guarantee to ~$120B; Rubin Ramp on Track
bullets.body: Nvidia downsized its financial backstop for the proposed OpenAI Ohio data center from $250B to under $120B to address balance-sheet risk concerns, with the first phase (~5GW) guarantee possibly signed as soon as the weekend. Separately, NVDA is in talks to invest $3B in SB Energy and disclosed a $21B SpaceX stake. MS maintains NVDA as top pick citing $1T Blackwell+Rubin demand visibility CY25–27 and 17x FY28 EPS; UBS and JPM both flag Rubin shipping Q3 with 150K units at ~$60K ASP. Pre-market, memory stocks (SNDK +4–5%, MU +3%, WDC +3–4%, STX +2%) led gains on Anthropic demand read-through.

bullets.title: Macro: Fed on Hold Through Year-End; Inflation Sticky But Not Re-Accelerating
bullets.body: MS and JPM both project Fed holds through year-end as base case; July core CPI printed +0.22% and core PCE is tracking ~0.20%, ruling out vol payback but insufficient to confirm trend. JPM's inflation forecasts show US headline CPI at 3.3% in Aug 2026 (down from 3.5% in June) with PCE headline at 3.8%. Retail sales missed significantly in July (-0.6% vs +0.1% consensus), but trailing 3-month sales are +6.3% YoY—JPM views the miss as overstated consumer weakness. Jackson Hole speech by Chair Warsh is flagged as key near-term catalyst for Fed reaction function.

bullets.title: Geopolitical Risk: Strait of Hormuz Shutdown, Iran-US Standoff, Israel-Hezbollah Escalation
bullets.body: Hormuz vessel transits ground to zero over the weekend with no crude shipments detected, and Iran's FM confirmed shipping will not resume until the US meets Tehran's core conditions. Brent crude rose ~1.7% to $88.52/bbl, up 40%+ YTD; WTI settled at $82.40. Separately, Israeli strikes killed 11+ in southern Lebanon and Hezbollah vowed retaliation. Kalshi markets price Hormuz normalization at 34% by Jan 1, 2027 and 49% by July 1, 2027; Polymarket has 17% odds of US military action against Iran before 2027.

bullets.title: Japan Yields Hit Multi-Decade Highs; China Data Misses Across the Board
bullets.body: Japan's 10-year JGB yield hit 2.91% (highest since 1996) and 2-year yield reached 1.69% (31-year high) on BOJ rate-hike bets; Q2 GDP printed +1.1% annualized (vs 2.0% est), which could prompt BOJ to hold. China July data missed on all fronts: industrial production +4.5% YoY (vs 5% est), retail sales +0.6% (vs 1.5% est), fixed assets -6.7% (vs -6.2% est), and property investment YTD -19.2%. Taiwan's 2026 GDP growth forecast was revised to 11.05%, first double-digit pace since 2010.

bullets.title: AI Hyperscaler Capex Flywheel: $3T Off-Balance-Sheet Commitments, $500B Financing Pool
bullets.body: Top 9 tech companies disclosed $3T in off-balance-sheet AI commitments; NVDA signed MOUs with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Goldman, KKR, and Brookfield to establish $500B GPU-financing capacity. IG companies sold nearly $1.5T bonds YTD (+36% YoY) with big tech accounting for ~$200B. Hyperscaler capex is projected to exceed $1.26T in 2027 and $1.4T in 2028 per Goldman. Morgan Stanley's AWS model sees a path to $1T revenue by 2034–35 assuming 8GW/year incremental capacity additions at $12–15/watt monetization; AMZN PT raised to $335 with bull case $500/share by YE2027.

bullets.title: Market Regime Shift to Growth Continuation; Momentum Unwind Seen as Opportunity
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (JPM, MS, 22V Research) flag a regime shift to 'Growth Continuation' favoring EPS momentum, value, and earnings growth over macro factors. The price momentum factor is unwinding after extreme concentration—~40% of top-decile momentum names are AI/tech-exposed—but the underlying fundamentals are intact. Hedge funds are returning to the Jan–April AI playbook: buying AI Winners (Semis, Memory) while selling Ex-AI names; JPM net exposure in hyperscalers moved from -1.5z to neutral (0z). Market breadth is broadening with RSP and IWM at ATHs.

bullets.title: NAND Shortage Worsening; Phison CEO Warns 2027 More Severe Than 2026
bullets.body: Phison's CEO projects 2027 NAND capacity constraints will be more severe than 2026, with upstream suppliers needing up to 4 years from plant construction to actual capacity. TLC spot prices began rising ahead of NVDA's Rubin ramp. SanDisk held an Investor Day projecting 80% adjusted gross margins through 2030 with LTAs covering 2/3 of 2028 output and $93B minimum contracted revenue. SNDK's persistent/long-horizon agent memory TAM was noted as excluded from prior guidance estimates.

bullets.title: JPM Raises S&P 500 PT to 8,000; Tactical Bullish Into NVDA Earnings Aug 26
bullets.body: JPM's chief equity strategist raised year-end S&P 500 price target to 8,000 from 7,800. The bank is tactically bullish with positive tech inertia ahead of NVDA earnings on August 26. FOMC minutes are due Wednesday; Flash PMIs expected at 53.5 (below street 53.9). Citi US Equity Strategy lifted 2026 EPS to $365 with year-end SPX target of 8,100; SPX options are pricing <55bps moves for the next 8 trading days (6th percentile). VIX closed at YTD lows on Friday.

bullets.title: Data Center Regulatory Pushback Spreading; Off-Grid Power Plays Favored
bullets.body: Texas ERCOT interconnection audit is viewed as a 1–3 month timing issue rather than demand destruction. Community opposition to data centers is scaling non-linearly with project size across Texas, Virginia, and Ohio. MS research favors onsite power providers (SEI, BE) and off-grid generation (WULF, GEV, CIFR) given grid uncertainty. Colocation operators (EQIX, DLR) are insulated by scale but face political headwinds that could redirect capacity to lower-friction jurisdictions. Texas is tracking ~100GW of planned data center capacity.

bullets.title: Retail Earnings Week Ahead: TGT, WMT, HD, LOW, TJX, ROSS, BURL
bullets.body: JPM raised TGT comp estimate to +3.5% (vs prior +1.8% and consensus +2.3%) calling it the best large-cap retail setup; WMT is a key test case with bulls at +3.5% US comps. HD expected to outperform LOW: HD US SSS +0.5–1% vs LOW near flat. ROST sentiment is robust (10–11% comps vs 7.6% consensus). July retail sales declined -0.6% vs +0.1% consensus on calendar shifts but trailing 3-month is +6.3% YoY. Consumer cash pile remains robust and lower-income wage growth is beating higher-income for first time since Dec 2024.

bullets.title: AI-Driven Optical Interconnect Demand Creates $100B+ Scale-Across Opportunity
bullets.body: DCI ports are projected to scale from <1M today to 20–40M by end of the decade, with ~30% tied to links stretching 100km+. Jefferies initiated NOK at Buy with €13.80 PT (59% upside), citing a €6.2B Cloud & AI backlog, 20x capacity expansion in San Jose fabs, and 800G Coherent Pluggable contracts with two hyperscalers (likely Meta and Google). Indium Phosphide substrate prices are rising 10%+ in Q4—the largest price hike on record—due to AI optical boom. Investors are pressing COHR to provide public data on UHP laser capabilities for CPO.

bullets.title: Software Sector Claws Back to Flat YTD; Silver Lake/WDAY Acquisition Speculation Elevated
bullets.body: Software (IGV) rallied to flat YTD with 3 consecutive weeks of outperformance vs Semis; infrastructure and security software averaged 9.6% and 4.3% post-earnings moves. Silver Lake is reportedly in talks to acquire WDAY at ~$230–245/share (~5x CY27 revenue), with skepticism on deal completion; Workday's CEO returned to pursue AI strategy and a sale before seeing ROI would be surprising (UBS). Software sector hire rates are bifurcated: app-layer AI companies doubled FDE hiring (116→208) while model labs halved theirs.

bullets.title: US-China AI Alignment War: US Drafts Allied Ultimatum; Apple Urged Off Chinese Memory
bullets.body: The US is preparing an ultimatum for allies to avoid joining China's AI ecosystem and is pressuring Apple not to source memory chips from CXMT or YMTC. Commerce Secretary Lutnick is involved in determining access to the proposed Ohio data center facility. BABA's Qwen models hit 3B+ global downloads (world's most downloaded), and Apple reportedly trained a China-specific LLM with Alibaba's support. NVDA's share of SK Hynix revenue fell from 24% in 2025 to ~13% in H1 2026 as hyperscalers accelerate internal chip development.

bullets.title: Q2 13F Filings: Major Institutions Piling Into GOOGL, Memory, AI Infrastructure
bullets.body: Berkshire added 48.1M GOOGL shares (now third-largest position at ~$37B); Druckenmiller initiated GOOGL and FOXA; Tiger Global added AMD and INTC; Altimeter opened MU and GOOGL. Situational Awareness (Leopold Aschenbrenner) filed with a 67% loss and margin calls, with largest positions SNDK (28.5%) and MU (28%). NVDA's 13F showed new COHR position and increased CRWV; top position INTC (~41%). Whale Rock (72% YTD) added ALAB and SNOW as new buys.

bullets.title: Homebuilder Risk Elevated; ITB Oct Puts Recommended as Hedge
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (22V Research, Hedgeye, JPM macro) note ITB (homebuilder ETF) is ~15–16% above May lows while 30-year mortgage yields are at or above May peaks (~5.25–5.26%). Two prior ITB/TLT spread peaks each resolved with 18–22% ITB drawdowns. Recommended trade: buy ITB Oct 16 $95 puts at ~$3. Housing affordability sits at the 25th historical percentile; mortgage rates at ~6.75%. Homebuilder trade is no longer favored given nominal GDP strength keeping 10-year yields elevated.

bullets.title: Private Credit Stress Rising; US Fiscal Deficit Hits Records
bullets.body: Private credit defaults hit a record in July and troubled loans reached 2017 levels. Big tech AI infrastructure bond and loan issuance hit $269B YTD (12x the 2015–2024 annual average and 2x all of 2025). The US fiscal deficit reached $1.8T in the first 10 months of FY2026, already exceeding all of FY2025; national debt is at $39.8T approaching $40T. US 30-year bonds were sold at highest borrowing costs since 2001; France's 30-year yield hit 4.85%, the highest since 2008.

bullets.title: China's Alibaba Pivots to AI: Qwen Downloads Surpass Meta, Gaming Unit Sold for $1.5B+
bullets.body: Alibaba's Qwen open-weight models accumulated 3B+ global downloads in six months, surpassing Meta and Alphabet to become the world's most-downloaded AI model. Alibaba agreed to sell Lingxi Games to Trustar Capital for $1.5B+ as part of its AI pivot. Berkshire Hathaway boosted its Alphabet stake by $17B in Q2 (now $36.6B, third-largest holding), a bullish signal on the AI monetization story.

bullets.title: Jane Street Posts ~$15B July Loss, First Negative Month Since 2016; Factor Unwind Cited
bullets.body: Jane Street executives told employees July was the first month of negative trading revenue since 2016, resulting in roughly a $15B loss attributed to Situational Awareness fund troubles and the rapid factor rotation in July from AI/momentum longs. The broad AI sector correction in July saw high-beta momentum swing from +69% YTD (June 22 peak) to negative YTD just five weeks later. Jane Street's YTD trading revenue remains $40B+ despite the July setback.

bullets.title: Stripe Acquires OpenRouter for $7B+; PayPal M&A Talks With Stripe and Advent
bullets.body: Stripe finalized an acquisition of OpenRouter, an AI model routing marketplace, for more than $7B (up from a $1.3B valuation months prior). Separately, PayPal is in talks to sell itself to a consortium including Stripe and Advent International, with PayPal having rejected a ~$53B offer as inadequate. The Stripe/OpenRouter deal positions Stripe to capture token billing, multi-model selection, and AI agent payments infrastructure.
